title: install named the launcher from the directory basename, verbatim
body:
# 0012: install named the launcher from the directory basename, verbatim

## Tags

install, naming, defaults, unix-convention, never-executed-path

## Summary

`devbin install` with no `--name` derived the project name from the target directory's basename and used it unchanged. That name becomes the launcher SYMLINK, so installing into `~/Devel/prj/Riffle` produced **`bin/Riffle`** -- a `bin/` entry with a capital letter, which is not a conforming Unix command name.

Reported by hv: *"Why is `~/Devel/prj/Riffle/bin/Riffle` (with a capital 'R'). That's non-conforming. I'd want to know why/how that happened because all bin scripts should be lower-case as per the Unix standard."*

## How it survived nine installs

Because the derivation had never once run on a capitalised directory.

| project      | directory      | project.name   | how                |
| ------------ | -------------- | -------------- | ------------------ |
| Conflab      | `Conflab`      | `conflab`      | explicit `--name`  |
| Laksa        | `Laksa`        | `laksa`        | explicit `--name`  |
| Baize        | `Baize`        | `baize`        | explicit `--name`  |
| Lamplight    | `Lamplight`    | `lamplight`    | explicit `--name`  |
| MicroGPTEx   | `MicroGPTEx`   | `microgptex`   | explicit `--name`  |
| Prolix       | `Prolix`       | `prolix`       | explicit `--name`  |
| arca_config  | `arca_config`  | `arca_config`  | **took the default** |
| arca_cli     | `arca_cli`     | `arca_cli`     | **took the default** |
| Riffle       | `Riffle`       | `Riffle`       | **took the default** |

All six capitalised projects happened to pass an explicit `--name`. Both projects that took the default already had lowercase directories, so the default was accidentally correct. **Riffle is the first install in the project's history to take the derived default on a capitalised directory**, and it got `bin/Riffle` on the first try.

This is the same shape as issues 0010 and 0011, all three found within the same week: a code path nothing had ever executed.

## Resolution

`lib/cmd/install`:

- The DERIVED default is lower-cased: `name="$(printf '%s' "${dstroot##*/}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"`.
- An EXPLICIT `--name` or `--alias` containing a capital is REFUSED at parse time, naming what it would have installed.

The split is deliberate. A derivation devbin performs is devbin's to get right silently; a value a person typed is an instruction, and quietly lowering it would hide the fact that the name they asked for is not one they can have.

Two tests, both red-checked first.

**The test could not assert what it wanted to assert, which is worth recording.** The obvious form is `refute_file_exists "$target/bin/Riffle"` -- and **APFS is case-insensitive, so that path resolves to `bin/riffle` and the assertion fails against a correct fix.** The test reads the STORED name instead:

    run bash -c "cd '$target/bin' && ls"
    assert_output_contains "riffle"
    refute_output_contains "Riffle"

Same filesystem property that already governs seal hand-cleans in this project (`find -name`, never shell globs).

## Notes

**Riffle's own repair needed three steps, not one, and two of them are not obvious.**

1. `bin/Riffle` renamed to `bin/riffle` -- hv did this, and **git did not see it.** `core.ignorecase=true` on macOS, so a case-only rename leaves `git status` clean while `git ls-files` still reports `bin/Riffle`. A fresh clone would have restored the capital. Forced with `git mv --force`.
2. `project.name` in `bin/.devbin/config.yaml` still read `Riffle`, so help still printed `Riffle -- dev launcher` and `bin/Riffle <command>`, and the dispatcher's own error text still pointed at `bin/Riffle help`. **The filename is downstream of config; renaming it alone fixes the listing and nothing else.**
3. Re-vendor, to take this fix.
